{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
    "line": 119,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Crash when Google Meet is the location and destinationCalendar is empty",
    "body": "In EventManager.create(), the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== \"google_calendar\"` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. If the event has Google Meet as its location but the organizer has no destination calendar (the array is empty or null), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError, aborting booking creation. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and was safe. This needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== \"google_calendar\"`."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
    "line": 1080,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Team destination calendars lost when organizer has no destination calendar",
    "body": "In handleNewBooking, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` — optional chaining on `null` silently skips the push, so the co-hosts' destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped entirely. In exactly the collective scenario this PR aims to fix, if the organizer (users[0]) has no destination calendar but co-hosts do, no calendar events will be created for the co-hosts. It should be `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 73,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Office365 creates every host's event in the main host's calendar",
    "body": "createEvent now always uses the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (`mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`) to build the URL `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events`. With multiple destination calendars (collective events), EventManager calls createEvent once per host credential, but this service ignores which credential it belongs to — unlike the Google service which matches `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. For a co-host's Office365 account, the main host's externalId is not valid in their account, so the API call fails (or worse, writes to an unintended calendar), and the co-host never gets the event. The same first-entry-only pattern in larkcalendar and BaseCalendarService (caldav) has the analogous problem: for non-main hosts the filter matches nothing, so no event is created at all while reporting success."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 256,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback find can never match",
    "body": "In updateEvent (and identically in deleteEvent at line ~317) the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the ternary's truthy branch returns it directly), so the find compares each calendar's externalId against undefined/null and always yields undefined. The previous behavior fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Result: when updateEvent/deleteEvent is called without an externalCalendarId, `calendarId` becomes undefined and the Google API call targets an undefined calendar. The fallback should use the first destination calendar's externalId (or match by credential) instead."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 168,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Hangout-link patch uses possibly undefined calendarId",
    "body": "In createEvent, the insert falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || \"primary\"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link to the description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. When no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the insert succeeds on \"primary\" but the patch is issued with `calendarId: undefined`, so the description update (containing the Meet link) silently fails."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts",
    "line": 151,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Unrelated logic inversion in organization creation",
    "body": "This PR about destination calendars also flips the condition for setting `slug` on organization creation: previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts which deployments store the slug directly on the team row vs. only as `requestedSlug` in metadata. If intentional it belongs in a separate PR with justification; as merged, self-hosted instances without team billing will stop persisting the organization slug, breaking org subdomain URLs."
  }
]}

findings.title: Crash when Google Meet is the location and destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: In EventManager.create(), the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. If the event has Google Meet as its location but the organizer has no destination calendar (the array is empty or null), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and accessing `.integration` throws a TypeError, aborting booking creation. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and was safe. This needs `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

findings.title: Team destination calendars lost when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: In handleNewBooking, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` — optional chaining on `null` silently skips the push, so the co-hosts' destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped entirely. In exactly the collective scenario this PR aims to fix, if the organizer (users[0]) has no destination calendar but co-hosts do, no calendar events will be created for the co-hosts. It should be `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: Office365 creates every host's event in the main host's calendar
findings.body: createEvent now always uses the first entry of `event.destinationCalendar` (`mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`) to build the URL `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events`. With multiple destination calendars (collective events), EventManager calls createEvent once per host credential, but this service ignores which credential it belongs to — unlike the Google service which matches `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. For a co-host's Office365 account, the main host's externalId is not valid in their account, so the API call fails (or worse, writes to an unintended calendar), and the co-host never gets the event. The same first-entry-only pattern in larkcalendar and BaseCalendarService (caldav) has the analogous problem: for non-main hosts the filter matches nothing, so no event is created at all while reporting success.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback find can never match
findings.body: In updateEvent (and identically in deleteEvent at line ~317) the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the ternary's truthy branch returns it directly), so the find compares each calendar's externalId against undefined/null and always yields undefined. The previous behavior fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Result: when updateEvent/deleteEvent is called without an externalCalendarId, `calendarId` becomes undefined and the Google API call targets an undefined calendar. The fallback should use the first destination calendar's externalId (or match by credential) instead.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: In createEvent, the insert falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link to the description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the fallback. When no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the insert succeeds on "primary" but the patch is issued with `calendarId: undefined`, so the description update (containing the Meet link) silently fails.

findings.title: Unrelated logic inversion in organization creation
findings.body: This PR about destination calendars also flips the condition for setting `slug` on organization creation: previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. This inverts which deployments store the slug directly on the team row vs. only as `requestedSlug` in metadata. If intentional it belongs in a separate PR with justification; as merged, self-hosted instances without team billing will stop persisting the organization slug, breaking org subdomain URLs.
